title: Identity vector record
description: One language-neutral conformance fixture for the identity projection and canonicalisation defined by the identity specification: a single input exercised against the identity algorithm, with its expected outcome. An input_bytes vector exercises the algorithm from the strict parse stage onward; an input vector is already-parsed JSON and exercises the algorithm from the schema-validation stage onward. See schemas/vectors/README.md for field semantics, the positive/negative split, and the failure-category vocabulary.

format_version.description: The vector record format's own version. Pinned to the version this schema validates; a vector claiming a different format_version must validate against that version's own schema instead. Distinct from identity_version and from the canonical definition's schema_version.

name.description: The vector's stable, unique, kebab-case id. Matches the stem of the file it lives in, so a file rename is a rename of the vector.

description.description: One-line, human-readable statement of what the vector proves.

identity_version.description: The identity_version this vector targets. Hashed as a domain separator, so a future identity_version's vectors are a new set validated against a new version of this schema, never mixed into this one.

classification.description: positive: the input canonicalises and mints an id. negative: the input is refused before minting, and no bytes or id exist to check.

coverage.description: Non-normative dot-separated tags naming what this vector exercises (e.g. "window.range.half-open-start", "entities.dedup"), used to check the suite's coverage against the coverage plan in schemas/vectors/README.md. Free to grow; not a frozen vocabulary like failure_category.

notes.description: Optional free-form context: why the vector is shaped this way, a pointer to the identity specification rule it enforces, or a caveat for a reader of the fixture.

input.description: The identity-core input as a parsed JSON value, pre-normalisation, used whenever the vector's outcome does not depend on the exact input bytes. Entity and role refs are already-canonical graph refs (alias resolution is out of this suite's scope). Mutually exclusive with input_bytes.

input_bytes.description: The exact UTF-8 bytes of the input document, lossless hex-encoded, executed against the strict parser. Required whenever the vector's outcome (success or failure) depends on input encoding: duplicate keys, lone surrogates, NaN/Infinity, out-of-range number literals, decomposed versus composed Unicode, or escaped-JSON forms. Mutually exclusive with input.

expected_projection.description: The fully normalised identity-core projection (the identity projection shape) the input must build, before JCS serialisation. Present only on a positive vector. Checks the normalisation and projection-building stages independently of the serialisation and hashing stages.

canonical_bytes.description: The exact JCS (RFC 8785) output bytes for expected_projection, lossless hex-encoded. Present only on a positive vector.

spec_id.description: The expected spec_id: "spec_" plus the first 32 lowercase hex characters of SHA-256(canonical_bytes). Present only on a positive vector.

failure_category.description: The stable failure category the input is refused under. Present only on a negative vector. See schemas/vectors/README.md for the frozen vocabulary and its citations.
